clue.text: OK character on page with mistakes about the boy Silver

indicators.note: the word for mistakes wraps around the boy and the silver

parts.note: errata are printed mistakes listed in a book
a son is a boy of the family
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A printed page full of errors concerning Long John Silver's young friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Silver' suggests the pirate from Treasure Island, but it is just the metal's symbol. ERRATA splits as ER...RATA around SONAG.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means a welcome or acceptable person, the opposite of one banned by a host country.

clue.text: Group of letters after uplifting talk

parts.note: post is Latin for after, used in English prefixes

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for talk is read upwards

parts.note: gab is idle talk

explanation.surface: A heap of mail arriving after an inspiring speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A postbag is the collection of letters a person or paper receives.

clue.text: Payment embracing dog not applicable — it's offensive

indicators.note: the payment word holds the dog and the abbreviation inside

parts.note: rent is a regular payment
a pug is a small breed of dog

explanation.surface: A rent demand that includes a pet charge, marked not applicable, causes outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Repugnant and offensive both describe something that provokes disgust.

clue.text: Zero degrees in the hot seat?

parts.note: O looks like zero
BA and MA are two university degrees, Bachelor and Master of Arts
BA and MA are two university degrees, Bachelor and Master of Arts

explanation.surface: Feeling the heat with zero degrees on the thermometer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degrees' suggests temperature, but it gives two academic degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: As US President he occupied the most pressured seat in the world when this was set.

clue.text: Herb — goddess gets one first

parts.note: Artemis is the Greek goddess of hunting
I is the Roman numeral for one
A denotes first, as in A grade

explanation.surface: A goddess comes first and takes a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemisia is the plant genus that includes wormwood, tarragon and mugwort.

clue.text: Demonstrate against 3 about right

indicators.note: the president's first name goes around the letter for right

parts.note: the answer to 3 down is the president whose first name is Barack

explanation.surface: Protesting against the President over a matter of rights.
explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference to 3 gives the surname; the wordplay needs the first name of the same man.
explanation.definitionFit: To barrack is to jeer or heckle a speaker, a form of demonstrating against them.

clue.text: Poet in a good year

indicators.note: the year abbreviation sits inside the word for good

parts.note: bon is French for good

explanation.surface: A poet producing work in a fine vintage year.
explanation.definitionFit: Lord Byron was a leading English Romantic poet.

clue.text: Endless worry with Skoda makes for restriction on travel

indicators.note: the letters are made into a new arrangement
the word worry loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Fretting over a Skoda car that slows the journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endless' cuts WORRY to WORR; 'makes for' rearranges WORR plus SKODA.
explanation.definitionFit: Repairs to the highway hold up traffic, so they restrict travel.

clue.text: Parcel out from Genesis to Malachi?

parts.note: Genesis is the first and Malachi the last book of the Old Testament, OT, so the span is all of it
Genesis is the first and Malachi the last book of the Old Testament, OT, so the span is all of it

explanation.surface: Sharing out portions across every book of the Hebrew scriptures.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute shares, to parcel out.

clue.text: Family flat, maybe, on Mull?

parts.note: kin are family
a tyre may be flat

explanation.surface: Relatives with a puncture on the Scottish island of Mull.
explanation.walkthrough: Mull is not the island here: the Mull of Kintyre is the headland at the peninsula's tip.
explanation.definitionFit: Kintyre is the Scottish peninsula whose southern headland is called its Mull.

clue.text: Brown ink

definitions.meaning: a reddish-brown colour, as in old photographs
the dark fluid squirted by cuttlefish, used as ink

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a warm brown tone and the cuttlefish secretion from which that pigment was made.

clue.text: Black stuff put on boy in sheet

parts.note: tar is black sticky stuff
Paul is a boy's name

explanation.surface: Someone smears tar on a lad lying in a bed sheet.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarpaulin is a large waterproof sheet of canvas used as a cover.

clue.text: One supplying drinks without food for the seventh stone

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the server's word goes round the food

parts.note: a barman serves drinks
an egg is an item of food

explanation.surface: A bartender working with nothing to eat, for a weight of seven stone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here, not lacking. Children count cherry stones with 'tinker, tailor, soldier, sailor, rich man, poor man, beggarman, thief'.
explanation.definitionFit: In the fortune-telling rhyme recited over plate leftovers, the seventh counted stone is the beggarman.

clue.text: Twig how to spell film actress 16's name?

definitions.meaning: a flexible willow shoot or stick

definitions.text: how to spell film actress 16's name?
definitions.meaning: the actress Jayne Mansfield spelt her first name with a Y rather than an I

explanation.definitionFit: A withy is a pliant willow twig, and the phrase split as two words describes Jayne's spelling.

clue.text: See 1
First class, sorely pressed, must be measured in knots

parts.note: A1 means first class, read as the letters A and I

indicators.note: sorely suggests being painfully twisted, signalling a rearrangement

explanation.surface: A top-quality item, badly squeezed, must be gauged in knots.
explanation.definitionFit: Aircraft speeds through the air are conventionally stated in nautical miles per hour.

clue.text: Insane medico having quarrel with piece of officer's kit

indicators.note: the word sane has the doctor and the quarrel inside it

parts.note: read as in sane: the word sane is the container
MB is a medical degree, so a doctor
a row is a quarrel

explanation.surface: A mad doctor arguing over a piece of military gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Insane' splits as 'In sane': MBROW goes inside SANE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sam Browne is a leather belt with a shoulder strap worn by army officers.

clue.text: Park Emma (to 25s) in Notts

parts.note: to Jane Austen fans, Park follows Mansfield in a novel title
Austen's heroine Emma's surname is Woodhouse

explanation.surface: An Austen novel and heroine placed in Nottinghamshire.
explanation.walkthrough: 25s are AUSTENITES, here Austen fans, not the iron phase. Notts is Nottinghamshire, an English Midlands county.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield Woodhouse is a town in the county of Nottinghamshire.

clue.text: See 16
A period in the wagon accessed by stopcock

indicators.note: the article and the period go inside the wagon

parts.note: a wain is an old word for a farm wagon
a term is a period of time

explanation.surface: A spell on the wagon, giving up drink, guarded by a tap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wagon' suggests being on the wagon, teetotal, which suits the water theme but is not the device.
explanation.definitionFit: A water main is a large supply pipe that is turned on and off by a stopcock.

clue.text: Pervert with funny hat on the way to cause grief

parts.note: to warp is to pervert or distort

indicators.note: the letters of hat are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: A twisted figure in a silly hat heading out to make trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: To be 'on the warpath' is to set out angrily for a fight.
explanation.definitionFit: A warpath is the route taken to make war, figuratively an angry course of action.

clue.text: Exclusive ice cream?

definitions.meaning: a news story one paper has to itself
a rounded ball of ice cream served by a spoon-like tool

explanation.definitionFit: A scoop is both a newspaper's exclusive story and a serving portion of ice cream.

clue.text: Cap given with approval to Fitzgerald

parts.note: a pat on the back shows approval
Ella Fitzgerald was the jazz singer

explanation.surface: A sporting cap handed to Fitzgerald with praise.
explanation.definitionFit: The patella is the kneecap, the bone capping the knee.

clue.text: Summing up number in harvest

indicators.note: the number is placed inside the word for harvest

parts.note: to reap is to harvest
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred, a number

explanation.surface: A tally of the figures gathered in at harvest time.
explanation.definitionFit: A recap is a summary, short for recapitulation, used of summing up what was said.

clue.text: Conspirator taking notes from waterfall

indicators.note: the notes are taken away from the waterfall word

parts.note: a cascade is a waterfall
D and E are musical notes

explanation.surface: A plotter lifting tunes from the sound of a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Casca was one of the conspirators who assassinated Julius Caesar.

clue.text: Trouble about meat with a crack

indicators.note: the word for trouble wraps around the word for meat

parts.note: a riot is civil trouble
flesh is meat

explanation.surface: Unrest breaks out over meat, punctuated by a gunshot.
explanation.definitionFit: The sharp report of a fired rifle is described as a crack.

clue.text: Call on reserves on such a day and get home in the light

definitions.text: Call on reserves on such a day

indicators.note: the word for home goes inside the light word

parts.note: a ray is a beam of light
in means at home

explanation.surface: Dip into savings on a wet day and head indoors.
explanation.walkthrough: Saving 'for a rainy day' means keeping reserves for a hard time.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom sets aside savings for a wet day, the time of need when reserves are used.

clue.text: Provide with English joke

parts.note: a quip is a witty joke

explanation.surface: An Englishman supplies the punchline.
explanation.definitionFit: To equip someone is to furnish or supply them with what is needed.

clue.text: Form of carbon in iron and gold, gun giving it energy

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold
the Sten is a British submachine gun
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A metallurgical recipe in which a weapon supplies the power.
explanation.definitionFit: Austenite is a solid solution of carbon in iron, a phase found in steel.

clue.text: Common Praise in Latin? Turn back

parts.note: a U-turn, so the letter U stands for a turn

indicators.note: the Latin word is written backwards

parts.note: laus is the Latin noun for praise

explanation.surface: A routine hymn of praise sung in Latin, then a retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Turn' gives U, as in U-turn; 'back' reverses LAUS to SUAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Usual and common are synonyms for what is ordinary or frequently met.

clue.text: Little bird will listen before speaking

indicators.note: the listening word comes ahead of the speaking word

parts.note: to hear is to listen
to say is to speak

explanation.surface: A small bird that listens before it chirps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A little bird told me' is said of gossip from an unnamed source.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumour passed on secondhand is attributed in the idiom to a small feathered informant.

clue.text: Immerse time and time flies

parts.note: to dip is to immerse briefly
an era is a period of time
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: Plunge something in, time and again, as the hours fly by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time flies' reads as the proverb, but 'flies' is a noun naming the insects.
explanation.definitionFit: Diptera is the insect order of two-winged true flies such as houseflies and mosquitoes.
